title: hand sth over: don't forget the "what"

card.wrong: Why don't you just ~~hand over to AI~~?
card.right: Why don't you just **hand your emails over** to AI?

why_en: hand sth over (to sb): say what you hand over · it / them always in the middle: hand it over · passive: it can be handed over.

items.o: My spreadsheets are a mess. I'd love AI to deal with them.
items.n: With a noun both orders work: hand my spreadsheets over / hand over my spreadsheets. With them — only in the middle: hand them over, not ~~hand over them~~.

items.o: AI could do most of our translation work now.
items.pre: Most of our translation work could

items.o: Never let AI write your wedding speech.
items.n: With a noun both orders work. With it / them — only in the middle: hand it over.

title: come in handy: with “in”

card.wrong: My first-aid course ~~came handy~~ last week.
card.right: My first-aid course **came in handy** last week.

why_en: come in handy = be useful when you need it — always with “in”.

items.o: Knowing a bit of Spanish was useful on holiday.
items.n: It helped at the time → came in handy.

items.o: Keep the box — we might need it one day.
items.n: It may help one day → might come in handy.

title: the hard way: no “in”

card.wrong: I learned it ~~in the hard way~~.

why_en: learn / find out sth the hard way = through your own mistakes — no “in”.

items.o: I only understood why backups matter after I lost all my photos.
items.n: or: I learned the hard way that you should always back up your photos.

items.o: Nobody told me the last bus leaves at 11. I found out at midnight, at the bus stop.
items.post: that the last bus leaves at 11.

title: have to: when there's no choice

card.wrong: When you move abroad, you ~~should~~ start from scratch.
card.right: When you move abroad, you **have to** start from scratch.

why_en: have to = there's no choice · should = it's a good idea (advice).
why_ru: have to = приходится (нет выбора) · should = стоит, лучше бы (совет)

items.o: In my job it's necessary to answer emails within an hour.
There was no lift, so the only option was to carry the sofa up five floors.
items.pre: There was no lift, so we
items.post: carry the sofa up five floors.

items.o: Is it really necessary for you to work this weekend?

title: came in handy or might come in handy?
why_en: It helped at the time → it came in handy. · It may help one day → it might come in handy.
why_ru: пригодилось (тогда) → came in handy · может пригодиться → might come in handy

items.q: Your phone died on the first day of your trip, but you had a power bank with you. Later you tell a friend:
opts: My power bank came in handy.
My power bank might come in handy.
items.n: It helped at the time → came in handy.

items.q: Before your trip to Japan, a friend gives you a phrasebook. You say:
opts: Thanks — that might come in handy!
items.n: It may help later → might come in handy. · or: That'll come in handy!
